rationale: I shot the town at seed 42, day 3, 10.4h and then MEASURED the shots rather than looking at them, because the last two bets that worked (#125's slate, #130's roofline) both came from a number and the ones that fizzled came from an impression. Classifying every canvas pixel back through project() into its ground class gives, as sd/mean over the class and share of a 1600x950 frame: ROAD 0.065 / 7.7%, GRASS 0.131 / 10.9%, PATH.court 0.143 / 9.3%, WATER 0.151 / 4.8%, SIDE.cross 0.185 / 4.1%, SIDE.quay 0.229 / 2.3%, WALL 0.240 / 12.3%. The roadway is three times flatter than the paving it runs beside, it is 7.7% of the frame, and it is the nearest big surface to the viewer — the one place LAWS says contrast should be HIGHEST. It is flat by construction and I found the two lines: groundBase's ROAD branch is the only ground colour whose hash term is halved (hv*0.5) over a pair six luma apart, and drawGround's ROAD branch strokes its setts at alpha .14 with off=(y%2)*0.5, so the bond alternates by row and never runs. That is #125's argument exactly — the biggest flat object in the picture, one iteration after the roof that held the title — and retiring a surface and laying it properly is rung 6 by name. The ladder did not force this climb (history 5, 6, 4b) and no signal is firing; the measurement forced it. The other four go to the four longest-untouched domains with every premise re-priced on HEAD by me, not by the cue that raised it: the quay really has no moorings and no hull ever ties there while the ticker has been saying 'a barge horn sounds somewhere far downstream' as one of its deliberately unplaced SOUNDS (b136, and it moves `structures`); LAWN_CAP is genuinely the only population cap whose knee has ever been swept, and the wide shot holds 42 people (b137); the plot lattice at ox 80..90 step 5 x oy 8..50 step 7 leaves a 1-cell way round every plot and there is not one shed, butt, cane or cloche on any of them (b138); and c205's 1.53 of GARDEN_ROWS 5 is #129's own measurement, so b139 arrives pre-counted and should be cheap. TWO PREMISES I KILLED BEFORE WRITING THEM: a brief about rain changing how people walk (coverF already puts umbrellas up before the first drop) and one about desire lines through the allotments (wear[] accrues on GRASS under every step in stepAgent, so they are already there). THE BUDGET, for the third time: it has been fixed at #119 and #124 and come back both times, so this pass I cut the file that is read MOST rather than the file that is biggest. LAWS.md was rewritten whole — nine laws promoted out of #130-#134 by MERGING into existing paragraphs (signature-widening into one-predicate; hash-is-not-seeded and hash-not-R-for-user-input into the R() law; clause-by-clause instrumentation into the rate-of-zero law; PAIR_GAP-all-round into the renderer traps; membership-drawn-per-sample into locate-before-you-judge; same-evaluate canvas reads and perf.mjs-is-vsync-blind into the probe law; the screen-cull rule into the framing law) and paid for by cutting roughly 1.9 KB of worked arithmetic from twelve laws, so it lands at 12,249 of 12,288 bytes with nine more claims in it than it had. queue.brief: The wide shot is a big town with a small population: at seed 42, day 3, 10.4h the frame holds 42 people across 138x88 of world. Every population cap in the town was chosen rather than measured except one — capacity, laneCap (peaks at 9 and feeds the WHOLE east half through a single spawnLaneAgent roll), eastCap (max 7), FAR_CAP 3, EVE_CAP, FAM_CAP — while LAWN_CAP is the only one whose knee has ever been swept, at #121, where the answer was 4 -> 8 and the sub-caps took over. Do for the town what #121 did for the lawn: measure presence per PLACE across a whole day rather than a per-instant crop, sweep the caps one at a time, find where each stops binding, name which sub-cap absorbs the slack, and keep the knee.
seams: LAWN_CAP and #121's sweep as the worked example
queue.successLooksLike: A presence-per-place table at each cap value on both builds, the knee named for every cap you moved, and a wide shot at the same pinned instant that reads as a busy town — with no place going from empty to crowded, the filmstrip clean, and figures still legible at 390x844.

queue.brief: Seventeen plots, a harvest cycle, a cart and a glasshouse — and not one tool. The allotments are the most worked ground in the town and carry no shed, no water butt, no bean canes, no cloche, no compost bay, no barrow: a plot is a rectangle of soil with a crop drawn on it. Give the plots their furniture on ROOF_FURN's model — a small set of pieces placed per plot off hash(plot), each one inside its own plot's rectangle (the lattice is ox 80..90 step 5 x oy 8..50 step 7, which leaves a 1-cell way round every plot), and each one named by the pointer the way roofFurnAt names the roof's. Let the set read the plot's own state: canes where something climbs, a cloche in the cold half of the year, a barrow only where somebody is working it, a butt against the fence.
seams: the plot lattice (the ox/oy loops near lines 3486 and 3510)
